title: MAG-S2: the shape of the quantum compass signal
description: Pre-registered simulation study of the shape of neural population activity that reads a radical-pair (cryptochrome) magnetic compass. The singlet yield of a radical pair is the same for a field and for the reversed field, so every cryptochrome signal and every neuron that sums such signals is an even function of the field direction, and the population lies on the real projective plane RP². A polarity-sensitive control read by the same eyes and neurons gives a sphere. Persistent homology with Z₂ and Z₃ coefficients tells the two shapes apart in recordings taken while three-axis coils rotate the field, without knowing what each neuron encodes. The protocol, code, physics and thresholds were frozen before the confirmatory run. In the confirmatory run on ten simulated birds (seeds 1–10, 7 November 2026) all invariants held and all expectations and hypotheses were met: the intact compass was labelled RP² in 10 of 10 birds, the polar control a sphere in 10 of 10, head rotations about the vertical axis a ring in 10 of 10 at inclination 66° and at the magnetic equator, and a nearest-neighbour heading decoder confused headings 180° apart at the equator (share of errors larger than 90° equal to 0.493, 95% interval 0.473–0.512) and kept them apart at inclination 66° (share 0). The release holds the frozen protocol (in Russian), the code with its synthetic tests, the computed physics, the confirmatory run with its verdicts, the calibration records, the pre-run checks and the figures.
